clinician.final_diagnosis: mucosal-dominant PV with minimal skin lesions
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 90-year-old Japanese woman presented with a 3-month history of painful gingivae, oral erosions, and difficulty eating. Intraoral examination revealed multiple erosions and desquamation with erythematous areas on the buccal mucosa, palate, tongue, and gingiva, with a positive Nikolsky’s sign. A few erythematous erosions were also noted on the back. A gingival biopsy showed intraepithelial cleavage with suprabasal acantholysis. Direct immunofluorescence revealed IgG and C3 deposition between epithelial cells. Serological testing showed elevated anti-desmoglein 3 (126 U/mL) and anti-desmoglein 1 (21 U/mL) antibodies. These findings collectively confirmed mucosal-dominant Pemphigus Vulgaris with minimal skin lesions.
